deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This controls what happens when Terraform removes the service. ABANDON removes it from Terraform management without deleting it from GCP, so a policy should block that value.

description.description: A human-readable description of the resource.
description.rationale: This is only a human-readable description. It does not change access, encryption, logging or network security.

disable_http2.description:
Disables HTTP/2.

HTTP/2 (h2) is enabled by default and recommended for performance. HTTP/2 improves connection re-use and reduces connection setup overhead by sending multiple streams over the same connection.

Some legacy HTTP clients may have issues with HTTP/2 connections due to broken HTTP/2 implementations. Setting this to true will prevent HTTP/2 from being advertised and negotiated.
disable_http2.rationale: This controls protocol compatibility and performance. Disabling HTTP/2 does not give a clear platform-level security improvement, so it should remain a team choice.

disable_quic.description: HTTP/3 (IETF QUIC) and Google QUIC are enabled by default.
disable_quic.rationale: This controls whether HTTP/3 and QUIC are available. It is mainly a protocol and performance choice, while TLS security is handled by other arguments.

edge_security_policy.description: Resource URL that points at the Cloud Armor edge security policy that is applied on each request against the EdgeCacheService.
edge_security_policy.rationale: This attaches a Cloud Armor edge security policy to requests reaching the service. A policy can require this value to be set without requiring one specific security policy.

edge_ssl_certificates.description:
URLs to sslCertificate resources that are used to authenticate connections between users and the EdgeCacheService.

Note that only "global" certificates with a "scope" of "EDGE_CACHE" can be attached to an EdgeCacheService.
edge_ssl_certificates.rationale: These certificates authenticate encrypted connections between clients and the service. Requiring at least one edge certificate supports secure HTTPS connections without fixing a team-specific certificate.

labels.description:
Set of label tags associated with the EdgeCache resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are only metadata used for organising and identifying resources. They do not change the security behaviour of the service.

name.description:
Name of the resource; provided by the client when the resource is created.
The name must be 1-64 characters long, and match the regular expression [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]* which means the first character must be a letter,
and all following characters must be a dash, underscore, letter or digit.
name.rationale: This is the resource identifier. A platform policy should not decide what a team names its resource.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This identifies the project that owns the resource. It is a project reference, and a generic policy should not require a specific project.

require_tls.description:
Require TLS (HTTPS) for all clients connecting to this service.

Clients who connect over HTTP (port 80) will receive a HTTP 301 to the same URL over HTTPS (port 443).
You must have at least one (1) edgeSslCertificate specified to enable this.
require_tls.rationale: This decides whether every client must use HTTPS. Requiring it to be true prevents clients from using an unencrypted HTTP connection.

ssl_policy.description:
URL of the SslPolicy resource that will be associated with the EdgeCacheService.

If not set, the EdgeCacheService has no SSL policy configured, and will default to the "COMPATIBLE" policy.
ssl_policy.rationale: This attaches an SSL policy to the service. If it is missing, Google uses the COMPATIBLE profile, so a policy should require an explicit SSL policy without fixing a specific resource.

log_config.description: Specifies the logging options for the traffic served by this service. If logging is enabled, logs will be exported to Cloud Logging.

log_config.enable.description: Specifies whether to enable logging for traffic served by this service.
log_config.enable.rationale: This controls whether service traffic is logged in Cloud Logging. Requiring logging gives visibility for monitoring, investigation and incident response.

log_config.sample_rate.description:
Configures the sampling rate of requests, where 1.0 means all logged requests are reported and 0.0 means no logged requests are reported. The default value is 1.0, and the value of the field must be in [0, 1].

This field can only be specified if logging is enabled for this service.
log_config.sample_rate.rationale: This controls how much service traffic is included in the logs. A rate of zero removes traffic visibility, so a policy can require a useful minimum sampling rate.

routing.description: Defines how requests are routed, modified, cached and/or which origin content is filled from.

routing.host_rule.description: The list of hostRules to match against. These rules define which hostnames the EdgeCacheService will match against, and which route configurations apply.

routing.host_rule.description.description: A human-readable description of the hostRule.
routing.host_rule.description.rationale: This is only a description of the host rule. It does not change which traffic is accepted or how the request is secured.

routing.host_rule.hosts.description:
The list of host patterns to match.

Host patterns must be valid hostnames. Ports are not allowed. Wildcard hosts are supported in the suffix or prefix form. * matches any string of ([a-z0-9-.]*). It does not match the empty string.

When multiple hosts are specified, hosts are matched in the following priority:

  1. Exact domain names: ''www.foo.com''.
  2. Suffix domain wildcards: ''*.foo.com'' or ''*-bar.foo.com''.
  3. Prefix domain wildcards: ''foo.*'' or ''foo-*''.
  4. Special wildcard ''*'' matching any domain.

  Notes:

    The wildcard will not match the empty string. e.g. ''*-bar.foo.com'' will match ''baz-bar.foo.com'' but not ''-bar.foo.com''. The longest wildcards match first. Only a single host in the entire service can match on ''*''. A domain must be unique across all configured hosts within a service.

    Hosts are matched against the HTTP Host header, or for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, the ":authority" header, from the incoming request.

    You may specify up to 10 hosts.
routing.host_rule.hosts.rationale: This controls which hostnames the service accepts. The unrestricted star host can match every domain, so a policy can block that broad pattern without requiring team-specific hostnames.

routing.host_rule.path_matcher.description: The name of the pathMatcher associated with this hostRule.
routing.host_rule.path_matcher.rationale: This is the name of another path matcher in the same routing configuration. It is an internal reference, not a security control.

routing.path_matcher.description: The list of pathMatchers referenced via name by hostRules. PathMatcher is used to match the path portion of the URL when a HostRule matches the URL's host portion.

routing.path_matcher.description.description: A human-readable description of the resource.
routing.path_matcher.description.rationale: This is only descriptive text for the path matcher. It does not control access or exposure.

routing.path_matcher.name.description: The name to which this PathMatcher is referred by the HostRule.
routing.path_matcher.name.rationale: This is an identifier used by the host rule. A platform policy should not control team-defined matcher names.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.description: The routeRules to match against. routeRules support advanced routing behaviour, and can match on paths, headers and query parameters, as well as status codes and HTTP methods.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.descript.description: A human-readable description of the routeRule.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.descript.rationale: This is only a description of the route rule. It does not change the route's security behaviour.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.origin.description:
The Origin resource that requests to this route should fetch from when a matching response is not in cache. Origins can be defined as short names ("my-origin") or fully-qualified resource URLs - e.g. "networkservices.googleapis.com/projects/my-project/global/edgecacheorigins/my-origin"

Only one of origin or urlRedirect can be set.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.origin.rationale: This points to the origin used by the route. It is a reference to another team-managed resource, so the referenced origin should be secured separately.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.priority.description:
The priority of this route rule, where 1 is the highest priority.

You cannot configure two or more routeRules with the same priority. Priority for each rule must be set to a number between 1 and 999 inclusive.

Priority numbers can have gaps, which enable you to add or remove rules in the future without affecting the rest of the rules. For example, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 12, 16 is a valid series of priority numbers
to which you could add rules numbered from 6 to 8, 10 to 11, and 13 to 15 in the future without any impact on existing rules.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.priority.rationale: This sets the order in which route rules are checked. The correct order depends on the team's routing design and cannot be decided by a generic security policy.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: The header actions, including adding & removing headers, for requests that match this route.
The name of the header to add.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This identifies a request header added by the route. Header names depend on the application, so a generic policy cannot choose the correct value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: The value of the header to add.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This is a free-form value added to a request header. Its correct value depends on the application and cannot be safely fixed by a generic policy.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: Whether to replace all existing headers with the same name.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This decides whether an existing request header is replaced. Whether replacement is correct depends on the selected header and the application's routing design.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: A list of header names for headers that need to be removed from the request prior to forwarding the request to the origin.
The name of the header to remove.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This identifies a request header removed before reaching the origin. The safe choice depends on the application's headers, so there is no universal value to enforce.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description:
Headers to add to the response prior to sending it back to the client.

Response headers are only sent to the client, and do not have an effect on the cache serving the response.
The name of the header to add.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This identifies a response header added by the route. The required headers depend on the application, so this field cannot be given one generic secure value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: The value of the header to add.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This is the value of a response header added to the client response. It is application-specific free-form data rather than a standalone security control.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: Whether to replace all existing headers with the same name.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This decides whether a response header with the same name is replaced. Its security effect depends on the header being changed.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.description: A list of header names for headers that need to be removed from the request prior to forwarding the request to the origin.

Headers to remove from the response prior to sending it back to the client.

Response headers are only sent to the client, and do not have an effect on the cache serving the response.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.header_a.rationale: This selects a response header to remove. Header requirements vary between applications, so a generic platform policy cannot safely choose the allowed names.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description:
The list of criteria for matching attributes of a request to this routeRule. This list has OR semantics: the request matches this routeRule when any of the matchRules are satisfied. However predicates
within a given matchRule have AND semantics. All predicates within a matchRule must match for the request to match the rule.

For satisfying the matchRule condition, the path of the request must exactly match the value specified in fullPathMatch after removing any query parameters and anchor that may be part of the original URL.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is an application path used to match incoming requests. Platform policy should not control team-defined URL paths.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: Specifies that prefixMatch and fullPathMatch matches are case sensitive.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This changes how paths are compared. The correct case behaviour depends on the application and does not provide a universal security improvement.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description:
For satisfying the matchRule condition, the path of the request
must match the wildcard pattern specified in pathTemplateMatch
after removing any query parameters and anchor that may be part
of the original URL.

pathTemplateMatch must be between 1 and 255 characters
(inclusive).  The pattern specified by pathTemplateMatch may
have at most 5 wildcard operators and at most 5 variable
captures in total.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is a team-defined path pattern used for routing. It does not have one generic secure value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: For satisfying the matchRule condition, the request's path must begin with the specified prefixMatch. prefixMatch must begin with a /.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is an application path prefix used to select a route. A platform policy should not decide the paths used by a team.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: Specifies a list of header match criteria, all of which must match corresponding headers in the request.
The value of the header should exactly match contents of exactMatch.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is an application-defined header value used for matching. There is no universal value that a platform policy can require.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: The header name to match on.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This chooses the request header used by a route match. The correct header depends on the application.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description:
If set to false (default), the headerMatch is considered a match if the match criteria above are met.
If set to true, the headerMatch is considered a match if the match criteria above are NOT met.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This reverses the result of a header match. Its effect depends on the full route rule, so the boolean alone is not a generic security control.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: The value of the header must start with the contents of prefixMatch.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is an application-defined header prefix used for routing. It does not have one platform-wide secure value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: A header with the contents of headerName must exist. The match takes place whether or not the request's header has a value.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This checks whether an application-specific header exists. Whether that check is needed depends on the route design.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: The value of the header must end with the contents of suffixMatch.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is an application-defined header suffix used for request matching. Platform policy should not control this routing value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: Specifies a list of query parameter match criteria, all of which must match corresponding query parameters in the request.
The queryParameterMatch matches if the value of the parameter exactly matches the contents of exactMatch.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is an application-defined query value used for routing. A generic policy cannot know the value each team needs.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: The name of the query parameter to match. The query parameter must exist in the request, in the absence of which the request match fails.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This is the name of a query parameter used by the application. It is a routing identifier rather than a platform security control.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.description: Specifies that the queryParameterMatch matches if the request contains the query parameter, irrespective of whether the parameter has a value or not.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.match_ru.rationale: This controls whether a route checks for the presence of a query parameter. The correct setting depends on the application's routing logic.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: In response to a matching path, the routeAction performs advanced routing actions like URL rewrites, header transformations, etc. prior to forwarding the request to the selected origin.

Setting the compression mode to automatic enables dynamic compression for every eligible response.

When dynamic compression is enabled, it is recommended to also set a cache policy to maximize efficiency. Possible values: ["DISABLED", "AUTOMATIC"]
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls response compression. It is mainly a performance setting and neither available value gives a clear platform-level security improvement.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: The policy to use for defining caching and signed request behaviour for requests that match this route.

Cache modes allow users to control the behaviour of the cache, what content it should cache automatically, whether to respect origin headers, or whether to unconditionally cache all responses.

For all cache modes, Cache-Control headers will be passed to the client. Use clientTtl to override what is sent to the client. Possible values: ["CACHE_ALL_STATIC", "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS", "FORCE_CACHE_ALL", "BYPASS_CACHE"]
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls how responses are cached. FORCE_CACHE_ALL can cache content even when the origin did not intend it, so a policy can block that risky mode.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Specifies a separate client (e.g. browser client) TTL, separate from the TTL used by the edge caches. Leaving this empty will use the same cache TTL for both the CDN and the client-facing response.

- The TTL must be > 0 and <= 86400s (1 day)
- The clientTtl cannot be larger than the defaultTtl (if set)
- Fractions of a second are not allowed.

Omit this field to use the defaultTtl, or the max-age set by the origin, as the client-facing TTL.

When the cache mode is set to "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS" or "BYPASS_CACHE", you must omit this field.
A duration in seconds terminated by 's'. Example: "3s".
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls how long clients cache content. The correct duration depends on how often the team's content changes, so it is a data-management choice.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Specifies the default TTL for cached content served by this origin for responses that do not have an existing valid TTL (max-age or s-max-age).

Defaults to 3600s (1 hour).

- The TTL must be >= 0 and <= 31,536,000 seconds (1 year)
- Setting a TTL of "0" means "always revalidate" (equivalent to must-revalidate)
- The value of defaultTTL cannot be set to a value greater than that of maxTTL.
- Fractions of a second are not allowed.
- When the cacheMode is set to FORCE_CACHE_ALL, the defaultTTL will overwrite the TTL set in all responses.

Note that infrequently accessed objects may be evicted from the cache before the defined TTL. Objects that expire will be revalidated with the origin.

When the cache mode is set to "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS" or "BYPASS_CACHE", you must omit this field.

A duration in seconds terminated by 's'. Example: "3s".
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls the default cache duration when the origin does not provide one. The correct value is based on the team's content and caching requirements.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Specifies the maximum allowed TTL for cached content served by this origin.

Defaults to 86400s (1 day).

Cache directives that attempt to set a max-age or s-maxage higher than this, or an Expires header more than maxTtl seconds in the future will be capped at the value of maxTTL, as if it were the value of an s-maxage Cache-Control directive.

- The TTL must be >= 0 and <= 31,536,000 seconds (1 year)
- Setting a TTL of "0" means "always revalidate"
- The value of maxTtl must be equal to or greater than defaultTtl.
- Fractions of a second are not allowed.

When the cache mode is set to "USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS", "FORCE_CACHE_ALL", or "BYPASS_CACHE", you must omit this field.

A duration in seconds terminated by 's'. Example: "3s".
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This limits how long content remains cached. It is a cache-management value and does not have one suitable platform-wide security limit.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Negative caching allows per-status code TTLs to be set, in order to apply fine-grained caching for common errors or redirects. This can reduce the load on your origin and improve end-user experience by reducing response latency.

By default, the CDNPolicy will apply the following default TTLs to these status codes:

- HTTP 300 (Multiple Choice), 301, 308 (Permanent Redirects): 10m
- HTTP 404 (Not Found), 410 (Gone), 451 (Unavailable For Legal Reasons): 120s
- HTTP 405 (Method Not Found), 414 (URI Too Long), 501 (Not Implemented): 60s

These defaults can be overridden in negativeCachingPolicy
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls whether common error responses are cached. It mainly affects origin load and performance rather than access or data protection.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Sets a cache TTL for the specified HTTP status code. negativeCaching must be enabled to configure negativeCachingPolicy.

- Omitting the policy and leaving negativeCaching enabled will use the default TTLs for each status code, defined in negativeCaching.
- TTLs must be >= 0 (where 0 is "always revalidate") and <= 86400s (1 day)

Note that when specifying an explicit negativeCachingPolicy, you should take care to specify a cache TTL for all response codes that you wish to cache. The CDNPolicy will not apply any default negative caching when a policy exists.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This sets cache durations for particular HTTP error codes. These durations are operational choices based on the application.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: The EdgeCacheKeyset containing the set of public keys used to validate signed requests at the edge.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This references the keyset used to validate signed requests. A platform policy should not require one team-specific keyset; signed-request enforcement is assessed separately.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Limit how far into the future the expiration time of a signed request may be.

When set, a signed request is rejected if its expiration time is later than now + signedRequestMaximumExpirationTtl, where now is the time at which the signed request is first handled by the CDN.

- The TTL must be > 0.
- Fractions of a second are not allowed.

By default, signedRequestMaximumExpirationTtl is not set and the expiration time of a signed request may be arbitrarily far into future.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This limits how far into the future a signed request can remain valid. Setting a maximum reduces the period in which a leaked or copied request can be reused.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Whether to enforce signed requests. The default value is DISABLED, which means all content is public, and does not authorize access.

You must also set a signedRequestKeyset to enable signed requests.

When set to REQUIRE_SIGNATURES, all matching requests will have their signature validated. Requests that were not signed with the corresponding private key, or that are otherwise invalid (expired, do not match the signature, IP address, or header) will be rejected with a HTTP 403 and (if enabled) logged. Possible values: ["DISABLED", "REQUIRE_SIGNATURES", "REQUIRE_TOKENS"]
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This decides whether cached content requires a valid signature or token. DISABLED leaves matching content public, so a policy can require signed requests for protected routes.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Enable signature generation or propagation on this route.

This field may only be specified when signedRequestMode is set to REQUIRE_TOKENS.
The actions to take to add signatures to responses. Possible values: ["GENERATE_COOKIE", "GENERATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS", "PROPAGATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS"]
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This selects how the service generates or passes tokens. The correct action depends on the application's media and token flow.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
The parameters to copy from the verified token to the generated token.

Only the following parameters may be copied:

  * 'PathGlobs'
  * 'paths'
  * 'acl'
  * 'URLPrefix'
  * 'IPRanges'
  * 'SessionID'
  * 'id'
  * 'Data'
  * 'data'
  * 'payload'
  * 'Headers'

You may specify up to 6 parameters to copy.  A given parameter is be copied only if the parameter exists in the verified token.  Parameter names are matched exactly as specified.  The order of the parameters does not matter.  Duplicates are not allowed.

This field may only be specified when the GENERATE_COOKIE or GENERATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS actions are specified.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This chooses which application token fields are copied into a generated token. The required fields depend on the team's token design.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
The keyset to use for signature generation.

The following are both valid paths to an EdgeCacheKeyset resource:

  * 'projects/project/locations/global/edgeCacheKeysets/yourKeyset'
  * 'yourKeyset'

This must be specified when the GENERATE_COOKIE or GENERATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS actions are specified.  This field may not be specified otherwise.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This is a reference to the keyset used for signature generation. Platform policy should not pin a specific team keyset.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
The query parameter in which to put the generated token.

If not specified, defaults to 'edge-cache-token'.

If specified, the name must be 1-64 characters long and match the regular expression '[a-zA-Z]([a-zA-Z0-9_-])*' which means the first character must be a letter, and all following characters must be a dash, underscore, letter or digit.

This field may only be set when the GENERATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS or PROPAGATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS actions are specified.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This names the query parameter used for a generated token. It is an application identifier and does not have one secure platform-wide name.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
The duration the token is valid starting from the moment the token is first generated.

Defaults to '86400s' (1 day).

The TTL must be >= 0 and <= 604,800 seconds (1 week).

This field may only be specified when the GENERATE_COOKIE or GENERATE_TOKEN_HLS_COOKIELESS actions are specified.

A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls how long a generated token remains valid. A policy can set a reasonable maximum so a leaked token cannot be reused for an unnecessarily long time.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: Defines the request parameters that contribute to the cache key.

If true, requests to different hosts will be cached separately.

Note: this should only be enabled if hosts share the same origin and content. Removing the host from the cache key may inadvertently result in different objects being cached than intended, depending on which route the first user matched.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This can remove the request host from the cache key. That may mix cached objects between different hosts, so a policy should keep the host separated.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
If true, exclude query string parameters from the cache key

If false (the default), include the query string parameters in
the cache key according to includeQueryParameters and
excludeQueryParameters. If neither includeQueryParameters nor
excludeQueryParameters is set, the entire query string will be
included.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This can remove the complete query string from the cache key. If query values change the response, removing them may serve one user's response to another request.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Names of query string parameters to exclude from cache keys. All other parameters will be included.

Either specify includedQueryParameters or excludedQueryParameters, not both. '&' and '=' will be percent encoded and not treated as delimiters.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This contains application-specific query parameter names excluded from cache keys. A generic policy cannot know which parameters affect each team's content.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: If true, http and https requests will be cached separately.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This decides whether HTTP and HTTPS requests use separate cache entries. Keeping the protocol in the cache key prevents content from different schemes being mixed.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Names of Cookies to include in cache keys.  The cookie name and cookie value of each cookie named will be used as part of the cache key.

Cookie names:
  - must be valid RFC 6265 "cookie-name" tokens
  - are case sensitive
  - cannot start with "Edge-Cache-" (case insensitive)

  Note that specifying several cookies, and/or cookies that have a large range of values (e.g., per-user) will dramatically impact the cache hit rate, and may result in a higher eviction rate and reduced performance.

  You may specify up to three cookie names.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This lists application cookies included in the cache key. Cookie names are team-specific, so a platform policy cannot require a particular list.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Names of HTTP request headers to include in cache keys. The value of the header field will be used as part of the cache key.

- Header names must be valid HTTP RFC 7230 header field values.
- Header field names are case insensitive
- To include the HTTP method, use ":method"

Note that specifying several headers, and/or headers that have a large range of values (e.g. per-user) will dramatically impact the cache hit rate, and may result in a higher eviction rate and reduced performance.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This lists application headers included in the cache key. The correct headers depend on which values change the response.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Names of query string parameters to include in cache keys. All other parameters will be excluded.

Either specify includedQueryParameters or excludedQueryParameters, not both. '&' and '=' will be percent encoded and not treated as delimiters.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This lists query parameters included in the cache key. The correct list depends on the application and cannot be set generically.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Additional options for signed tokens.

signedTokenOptions may only be specified when signedRequestMode is REQUIRE_TOKENS.

The allowed signature algorithms to use.

Defaults to using only ED25519.

You may specify up to 3 signature algorithms to use. Possible values: ["ED25519", "HMAC_SHA_256", "HMAC_SHA1"]
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls the algorithms accepted for signed tokens. A policy can allow strong options such as ED25519 and HMAC SHA-256 while blocking HMAC SHA-1.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
The query parameter in which to find the token.

The name must be 1-64 characters long and match the regular expression '[a-zA-Z]([a-zA-Z0-9_-])*' which means the first character must be a letter, and all following characters must be a dash, underscore, letter or digit.

Defaults to 'edge-cache-token'.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This is the application-defined name of the query parameter containing the token. The parameter name does not decide the token's security.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: CORSPolicy defines Cross-Origin-Resource-Sharing configuration, including which CORS response headers will be set.

In response to a preflight request, setting this to true indicates that the actual request can include user credentials.

This translates to the Access-Control-Allow-Credentials response header.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This decides whether cross-origin requests can include user credentials. Allowing credentials increases exposure, so a policy can require this to remain disabled.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: Specifies the content for the Access-Control-Allow-Headers response header.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls which request headers a browser may send across origins. A policy can block an unrestricted wildcard while leaving specific application headers to the team.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: Specifies the content for the Access-Control-Allow-Methods response header.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls which HTTP methods browsers may use across origins. A policy can prevent unrestricted or unnecessary write methods from being exposed.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Specifies the list of origins that will be allowed to do CORS requests.

This translates to the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls which origins can make cross-origin requests. A policy should block the unrestricted star origin to reduce accidental public browser access.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: If true, specifies the CORS policy is disabled. The default value is false, which indicates that the CORS policy is in effect.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: Disabling CORS is restrictive rather than publicly exposing the route. Whether the application needs CORS is a team design choice.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: Specifies the content for the Access-Control-Allow-Headers response header.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls which response headers browser code can read across origins. A policy can prevent wildcard exposure while allowing required headers to be selected by the team.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Specifies how long results of a preflight request can be cached by a client in seconds. Note that many browser clients enforce a maximum TTL of 600s (10 minutes).

- Setting the value to -1 forces a pre-flight check for all requests (not recommended)
- A maximum TTL of 86400s can be set, but note that (as above) some clients may force pre-flight checks at a more regular interval.
- This translates to the Access-Control-Max-Age header.

A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, terminated by 's'. Example: "3.5s".
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This controls how long a browser caches a CORS preflight decision. A reasonable maximum reduces how long an old permission remains active after a policy change.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: The URL rewrite configuration for requests that match this route.
Prior to forwarding the request to the selected origin, the request's host header is replaced with contents of hostRewrite.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This replaces the host header before forwarding the request to the selected origin. The required host is application-specific and cannot be chosen by platform policy.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description: Prior to forwarding the request to the selected origin, the matching portion of the request's path is replaced by pathPrefixRewrite.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This rewrites part of the application URL path. It is routing logic and does not have one generic secure value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.description:
Prior to forwarding the request to the selected origin, if the
request matched a pathTemplateMatch, the matching portion of the
request's path is replaced re-written using the pattern specified
by pathTemplateRewrite.

pathTemplateRewrite must be between 1 and 255 characters
(inclusive), must start with a '/', and must only use variables
captured by the route's pathTemplate matchers.

pathTemplateRewrite may only be used when all of a route's
MatchRules specify pathTemplate.

Only one of pathPrefixRewrite and pathTemplateRewrite may be
specified.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_ac.rationale: This rewrites an application path using captured variables. The correct template depends on the team's route design.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_me.description:
Allow overriding the set of methods that are allowed for this route.
When not set, Media CDN allows only "GET", "HEAD", and "OPTIONS".

The non-empty set of HTTP methods that are allowed for this route.

Any combination of "GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "PUT", "POST", "DELETE", and "PATCH".
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.route_me.rationale: This defines the HTTP methods required by the application route. The correct methods depend on whether the service supports read or write operations.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.description: The URL redirect configuration for requests that match this route.
The host that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.rationale: This is the team-defined host used in a redirect. A generic policy cannot require one particular hostname.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.description:
If set to true, the URL scheme in the redirected request is set to https. If set to false, the URL scheme of the redirected request will remain the same as that of the request.

This can only be set if there is at least one (1) edgeSslCertificate set on the service.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.rationale: This decides whether redirected clients are moved to HTTPS. Requiring it to be true prevents the redirect from keeping an unencrypted HTTP scheme.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.description:
The path that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request.

pathRedirect cannot be supplied together with prefixRedirect. Supply one alone or neither. If neither is supplied, the path of the original request will be used for the redirect.

The path value must be between 1 and 1024 characters.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.rationale: This is an application-defined destination path. Platform policy should not decide a team's URL structure.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.description:
The prefix that replaces the prefixMatch specified in the routeRule, retaining the remaining portion of the URL before redirecting the request.

prefixRedirect cannot be supplied together with pathRedirect. Supply one alone or neither. If neither is supplied, the path of the original request will be used for the redirect.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.rationale: This is an application-specific path prefix used during a redirect. It does not have one generic secure value.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.description:
The HTTP Status code to use for this RedirectAction.

The supported values are:

- 'MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT', which is the default value and corresponds to 301.
- 'FOUND', which corresponds to 302.
- 'SEE_OTHER' which corresponds to 303.
- 'TEMPORARY_REDIRECT', which corresponds to 307. in this case, the request method will be retained.
- 'PERMANENT_REDIRECT', which corresponds to 308. in this case, the request method will be retained. Possible values: ["MOVED_PERMANENTLY_DEFAULT", "FOUND", "SEE_OTHER", "TEMPORARY_REDIRECT", "PERMANENT_REDIRECT"]
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.rationale: This selects the HTTP status used for the redirect. The correct code depends on the application's required redirect behaviour.

routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.description: If set to true, any accompanying query portion of the original URL is removed prior to redirecting the request. If set to false, the query portion of the original URL is retained.
routing.path_matcher.route_rule.url_redi.rationale: This decides whether query values are removed from the redirected URL. Requiring removal helps prevent tokens or other sensitive query data being forwarded to another location.
